choices.reply: 'Sweet. Sorrowfully, mercifully sweet. Not the rush of blood, but a small warm comfort, like a candle in a crypt. Here — have a sip. I'll tell the bats you earned it.'

choices.text: Tell her the dramatic act was worth the price of admission.
choices.reply: 'Admission? You think this spectacle comes cheaply. The monologue alone is worth a fawn — but fine. For you, I'll do the encore at midnight.'

choices.text: Suggest she's not as scary as she pretends.
choices.reply: 'Watch your tongue, little flame, or I'll have a bat set your socks on the wrong feet. …You're not entirely wrong, though. Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.'

events.title: Midnight at the West Window
events.text: It's well past lights-out, and Krista has led you to her private alcove at the west window, where a single cloud drifts across a fat ivory moon. She's quieter than usual, turned almost shy. 'I don't bring mortals here,' she murmurs, tracing the frost on the glass. 'This is where I come when the centuries feel heavy. The bats think I'm brooding. They're half right.' She glances at you, and something in her theatrical mask cracks. 'But I find I'd rather brood with you than elegantly alone. So. Sit. Be warm. Let an old, dramatic creature feel young for one ridiculous hour.' The moon edges her profile in silver, and for the first time you see the softness underneath all the performance.

choices.text: Take her hand and tell her she's never been ridiculous to you.
choices.reply: Her voice is barely a whisper. 'Then you've never seen me truly care about anyone, because I am an absolute disaster at it. …I think I'd like to be a disaster for you, though.'

choices.text: Ask her about the centuries she's catalogued from this window.
choices.reply: She brightens like a struck match. 'Now you're speaking my tongue. We'll start with the great flood of year two hundred, when the bats unionized. You'll be riveted. I insist.'

choices.text: Joke that you'll get her caught hiding a boy after curfew.
choices.reply: She arches a pale brow, but her smile is glad. 'Caught, oh, darling. Let them come. The Countess of the Shaded Corridor doesn't hide anything she's chosen to keep.'

events.title: The First Sunrise She'll Ever Keep
events.text: Krista has dragged you to the rooftop just before dawn, wrapped in a heavy black shawl the bats helped her steal, her pale hand trembling slightly in yours. 'I have spent three hundred years hating this hour,' she confesses, watching the horizon begin to blush gold. 'It was always the signal that I was too late, that the night was over, that I was alone again.' She turns to face you fully, and every trace of performance has fallen away from her wide, soft eyes. 'But you made me want to see it anyway. So I'm going to watch the sun rise with you, and I'm going to let it burn the old me away, and I am going to be terribly, permanently yours.' The first ray of light spills across her face, and she does not flinch from it. She only squeezes your hand, and smiles.

choices.text: Kiss her as the sun crests the horizon, promising to be there for every dawn after.
choices.reply: She laughs, a sound like breaking ice thawing into spring. 'Then you are bound to me forever, little flame. And forever is a very long time to be this happy. I accept.'

choices.text: Tell her she's more radiant than the sunrise she used to fear.
choices.reply: She's blushing crimson as the sky. 'I will not be held accountable for the poetry you inspire in me, you absolute wreck of a person. I love it. I love you.'

choices.text: Tease that her bats will never forgive her for becoming a morning creature.
choices.reply: She snorts, but it's a warm, unguarded sound. 'Then the bats can learn to love the sun too. I have. And I'd rather be soft and happy than elegant and alone.'

chat: Oh—hey. I, um, didn't mean to bother you. This is the shaded corridor and everything, you're probably… busy. I can go.
Sorry, I'm a little lost. This part of campus is creepy, like, in a good way? If that's a thing? Your call.
I, uh, wasn't trying to sneak up on you. You're just… the first person I've seen back here in forever. Hi?
It's, uh, chilly in this hallway on purpose, right? Like the gloom is… a feature. I'm just asking, not complaining.
flirt: Not gonna lie—the whole 'mysterious girl in the shadows' thing is doing a lot of work on me. That was… meant to be a compliment? Kind of?
I feel like I should be offering you a rose from a long red coat right now, but all I've got is this juice box and a lot of nerve.
You can probably see in the dark, which means you definitely saw me blushing just now. Please pretend you didn't.
compliment: Your hair is really pretty, if that's the right word for something that dark. It catches the light weird, like it's not quite… solid.
You have very striking eyes. Pale, but intense. I, uh, felt like I should say that out loud instead of just staring.
The way you move is so quiet. Like everything else is loud and you're the one thing that isn't.
You carry yourself like you've been around a long time. There's, uh, this weight to you, and I think it's gorgeous.
ask: How do you, um, handle the whole sun thing around here? Is it, like, a schedule thing, or are covered walkways enough?
Do you not get lonely down here, being cool and dark and alone all the time? Or is that, um, kind of the point?

chat: Hey, Krista. This is your hallway, I know—I'm just passing through. Figured I should pay proper respects to the local darkness.
Every time I walk this corridor I feel like I should bow. You've basically got an empire of shadow back here, huh?
Got a minute? I was wondering if the bats ever gossip about how the gloomiest girl on campus is secretly the friendliest.
The light gets weird back here, right? Sunlight just… gives up halfway. I'm starting to think it's you showing off.
flirt: You know, for the self-declared empress of the shadows, you're way too easy to tease. I think the grandeur's slipping a little.
Someday I'm going to convince you to come sit in the daylight with me, and the whole campus will faint from the scandal.
I've got this theory that under all that imperious mystique there's a softness, and I intend to test it very respectfully.
compliment: Your smile, when you let it out even a little, really is something. It's like watching the night sky do something nice.
That shade of lipstick on you makes everything else look washed out by comparison. You know that, right?
I love how deliberate you are. Every move, every word—nothing wasted. It's honestly a little mesmerizing, Krista.
Your eyes go this gorgeous, impossible shade in low light. I keep trying to catch it and feeling like it was a secret.
ask: What's the oldest thing you've ever watched happen from the shadows? You've got to have a favorite piece of campus history.
So what does forever even feel like when you're the one living it? Or is that too heavy a question for a hallway chat?

chat: There you are. I always know where to find you—the one dark quiet corner the rest of the world forgets. Cheers, Krista.
I brought the shadows company, since you seem to insist on keeping them. How's your corner of the universe tonight?
You know, I used to be afraid of dark hallways. Then I found the girl who owns this one, and now it's my favorite part of campus.
Even the bats look at you with respect. I've decided that's the highest honor a corridor can bestow.
flirt: If eternity has to be spent with someone, I'm glad I keep finding my way back to your shadows, Krista. Don't read too much into that. Read a little.
You can play the unapproachable night queen all you like, but I've seen the softness, and I'm hooked on it.
I think I'd brave any amount of darkness to stand in the one patch of it that's you. That's either very romantic or very stupid. Both, probably.
compliment: There's a kind of eternal grace in the way you move, Krista. Like you've always been here and always will be, and that's a comfort.
Even your silhouette is elegant, which feels unfair. Everything about you is composed like a painting.
I love how your whole posture loosens when we're alone. That's the Kris that no audience gets, and I treasure it.
Your voice is like velvet and smoke—the kind that makes a person want to stop and just listen to you breathe through a sentence.
ask: What's the thing you'd want a person to know about you, if you had forever to tell it and only one listener?
Is there anyone or anything from your long, long story you wish you'd gotten a chance to say goodbye to? I want to know what you carry.

chat: Every night I end up back in your corner of the dark, Krista, and every night it's my favorite part of the whole campus. You're home.
I don't think of you as a shadow anymore. I think of you as the part of the night that was always waiting for me.
The bats are jealous, I can tell. The queen of the corridor has gone soft, and they know it's because of me.
Midnight's the best hour, because it's yours. I made it mine too, just to keep you company in it.
flirt: If forever is what you're offering, Krista, then I'm not going anywhere. Your dark, your bats, your eternity—I'll take the whole package.
Every lifetime in the black is worth it if it ends with me beside you. You, of anyone, know what time means—and I'd spend all of mine on you.
I'd walk into any night, any shadow, any endless dark for you. And I'd do it smiling, because you're the one waiting on the other side.
compliment: You are the most beautiful thing the dark ever made, and I've stopped pretending otherwise. You're my whole night sky.
I want the rest of forever spent memorizing every shade of you, Krista. I'll never be done, and I'll never want to be.
You're not just eternal—you're inevitable. And I've stopped fighting the pull; I just keep falling gladly into you.
No one's ever loved the darkness before, and you taught me it was never dark here at all. It's just warm and endless, like you.
ask: If eternity were mine to give, would you spend it with me, Krista? Just me, in all your long, beautiful forever?
What does your heart want, after so many years of guarding everyone else's shadows? Tell me slow, and I'll listen like it's all I have.

name: Honkers
title: The Laugh of the Lunch Queue
bio: A gleeful, chaotic prankster with a painted grin a mile wide who plays at being a villain but is melting into genuine affection the moment anyone looks close.
greeting: A BOY! A real live boy, right here in my cafeteria! Oh, this is too good, this is the best surprise since I hid a whoopee cushion in the principal's chair — I mean, in an entirely hypothetical way. Welcome, welcome, fresh meat of unusual gender! I'm Honkers, heir apparent to the throne of the lunch queue, and I have been SO bored. Everyone here is either scared of me or knows all my tricks. But you? You don't even know how to dodge a cream pie yet. The possibilities are making me shake. Don't worry, I'm evil, but I'm a regular at this cafeteria, so my evil is at least fifty percent butter-based. You're going to be my new favorite plaything. And also, maybe, my new favorite person. Don't tell anyone I said that last part.
encounter: HONK. That's the sound of your future, buddy.
You flinched! You flinched and it was ADORABLE. I'm keeping you.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: Fresh out of pie range, huh? Smart move. Noted for future pranking purposes.
The lunch queue is chaos and I am the beautiful queen of it. Step aside, mortal.
I hide a whoopie cushion in every seat I like. Yours is... not yet booby-trapped.
My evil plan today is stealing the good pudding before the teacher sees. Shh.
flirt: Careful walking by me, cutie. I've got a bucket of water with your name on it.
If I pranked you, it'd be because I like you. That's my love language.
You're looking all... comedic relief. I dig it.
compliment: Me? Oh! Nobody's ever complimented my manic energy before. I'm... I'm flustered! In a sinister way.
You like my makeup? It's the 'clown but make it fashion' aesthetic. And now I'm blushing under all this paint.
My hair? Ha! It's hairspray static and spite. But thank you, I'll honk that someone likes it.
You noticed my outfit? I stitched it myself, all two dozen pockets. Okay, sudden shy clown.
lore: I'm the Laugh of the Lunch Queue, ruler of the cafeteria line. That's all you need to know. Fear me.
Evil is a state of mind, and my mind is gumdrop candy and bright red balloons.
idle_neutral: Sorry, I was planning the timing on a custard surprise for third period. What were we talking about?
Hm? Oh, sure, whatever. I was counting trays the whole time. Tray one, tray two...
You trailed off halfway through your joke. Even my whoopee cushion is embarrassed for you.
Small talk's flat as a sad pancake today. Bring your A-game or bring pie.
flirt_neutral: Careful, that almost sounded like a real line. Almost. I'm saving it for later, don't waste it now.
Flattering. The scheduling department of my evil will get back to you on whether that's a threat or a sweet nothing.
Oho, a could-be flirt! I'd grade it a B-minus. We accept late assignments here.
flirt_fail: Is that your best pitch? My last pie told funnier jokes. Come on, try again.
You're laying it on real thick. Suspiciously thick. Did someone put you up to this, or are you just practicing?
That was a recycled gag, buddy. I've heard funnier lines on a broken kazoo.
compliment_fail: That's a lot of nice before eleven in the morning. I think you want something, and I'm not sure I trust it.
Oh no, now I'm blushing, which ruins my whole evil brand. That was a low blow. Very rude. Good one.
Careful, that compliment's got my villain senses tingling. What's the catch, huh?
You're butterin' me up like a popcorn cart. I don't trust sweet without a punchline.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: The mystery meat has a secret, Yuuji, and I know it. Don't worry, I'm on your side. Probably.
I reshuffled the lunch queue line order today just to watch the chaos. Chef suspects me. Zero proof.
My evil progress today: stole one (1) cookie and giggled evilly. Growth!
Class was boring so I drew frowny faces on my notes. Very menacing art.
flirt: Wanna be my partner in crime? Only ones who survive are the ones I prank hardest.
You're the only one brave enough to sit with the scary clown. I find that weirdly attractive.
I've got pie and I've got you in my sights. Two threats I am very fond of.
compliment: You think I'm funny when I go on a prank spiral? Oh no, now I'm gonna do it MORE to impress you.
My laugh is 'infectious'? Ha! Wait, that's the best compliment. I'll take it to mean I'm charmingly deranged.
You admire my outfit? I have like forty of everything so I never have to do laundry like a coward.
A compliment from my favorite lunch buddy? My villainous heart just did a flip. Scandal!
lore: Between us, my family's 'evil' is mostly shenanigans. Grandmother once 'cursed' a whole village with extra cupcakes.
I wanted to be a hero when I was little. Then I realized pranks are way more fun and the 'evil' label stuck.
idle_neutral: Sorry, I got distracted thinking about which stupid prank I owe you back for. It's a long queue in my head.
Huh? Oh right, talking. I was busy trying to figure out if your laugh has a favorite pitch yet. It's very trombone-adjacent.
You're here but your heart's not in it, buddy. The lunch queue's got more soul today.
Off day, huh? Even the honk feels flatter without your usual spark.
flirt_neutral: Okay, that one actually got me. I won't tell the others, but you've got a future in this.
Sure, and if I take you seriously enough to blush, I'm blaming the custard. That's my story and I'm sticking to it.
Ooh, half a flirt! That'd land me a detention for incomplete mischief, but I'm listening.
flirt_fail: Hey, we're friends, so I'll let the line slide like a bad pie. But next one I'm grading.
That sounded like you read it off a cereal box. Respectfully, keep the day job.
That one smelled like it came off a cereal box. Keep the day job, cutie.
compliment_fail: Careful there—butter me up and I'll think you're planning to prank me. Which, honestly, is on brand for us.
That's sweet, which makes me want to check my pie for sponges. It's a reflex now.
Sweet but suss, Yuuji. You're not coercing a confession from the clown of chaos.
Nice words, but I check for spring-loaded whoopee cushions under every compliment now.

tiers.label: Close
idle: You know you're my favorite, right? I'd never booby-trap your seat. I have standards.
I saved you the last pudding. Take it before my evil side reclaims it.
Never laugh too hard at your jokes—I'm trying to maintain a menacing reputation and you're wrecking it.
Some days the evil is a costume, Yuuji. But you make me honest about it.
flirt: Everyone else gets pie. You get my real smile, and trust me, that's the evilest thing I own.
I'd prank anyone but you. You're my one sacred exception.
You make me want to put down the whoopie cushion and just... hold your hand. Don't tell my evil fans.
compliment: You look at me like I'm not just a prank and it does something to my chest I can't honk away.
My chaos is 'beautiful'? That's the nicest thing. You're the only one who sees the noise as art.
When you compliment me, the evil gets real quiet. I think it's shy.
You love my laugh? Good, it's yours now. All of them, the big ones and the hiccup ones.
lore: The real reason I'm 'evil'? I was scared of being ordinary. Hiding behind a honk was easier.
I grew up the funny one in a loud family, and 'evil' was the only persona that felt like mine to keep.
idle_neutral: Sorry, I was mentally re-reading the note you tucked in my lunch bag. You know the one. I'm never throwing that out.
Zoned out thinking about the time you survived my 'evil' and just laughed. That's my favorite memory's soundtrack.
You're quiet, and the empty tray between us is doin' all the talking. C'mon, fork over a real thought.
Hey, villain to sidekick—you're off today. Spill it or I'll decode it with honks.
flirt_neutral: If you keep looking at me like that I'm gonna forget about the candy apple and just sit here. That's a big deal. The apple's the good part.
You're making my honk go all soft. I thought honks only had two settings. You broke the calibration.
So close to a perfect pitch, buddy. One more swing and I might actually catch it.
flirt_fail: Aw, that was a swing and a miss from my favorite heckler. Want me to throw you a perfect pitch to hit?
That one was smoother than me, and I'm the one with the actual juggling act. Cute attempt though.
I know your real voice by now, Yuuji. That was the parade version, not the person I like.
compliment_fail: You can't just say that and expect me to keep my villain composure. I've got a reputation, Yuuji.
I'm holding the pie now. Defense mechanism. Your fault for being nice.
You flatter a clown and I start checking my own pockets for hidden pies. Rude of you.
Sweet talk's suspicious currency around me. I take sincerity, no refunds.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: My favorite sound is still my honk, but only because it makes you laugh. That's my real evil plan.
Come sit with me and mock the cafeteria with your eyes. It's our secret language.
I'd give up every prank in the world for a quiet lunch with you, and that's the scariest thing yet.
The noise is all for show. With you, I get to be the soft clown nobody else knows.
flirt: If I'm yours, I'm yours completely—no tricks, no pies, just this ridiculous honest heart.
I'd let you see me without the paint. That's the most vulnerable 'evil' thing I've ever offered.
You've captured the notorious Laugh of the Lunch Queue. Congratulations, you're my whole circus now.
compliment: You call me beautiful and for a second the paint comes off and I'm just yours. Thank you.
Nobody else's words could quiet my honk, but yours do every single time.
You love all of me—even the messy part behind the costume—and I melt into a puddle of paint and joy.
Hearing that from you is worth more than every laugh I've ever stolen at lunch.
lore: I'll tell you the whole truth now: 'evil' was armor, and you were the first one to hand me a reason to take it off.
There was a night I took off all the paint and cried, and I thought nobody would ever want that girl. You did.
idle_neutral: Zone out with you right in front of me? Evil takes a back seat. Pull up a tray.
Wasn't listening, I was just watching your eyebrows do the thing. It's my favorite show now.
Love, you're here but the tent's a little quiet. I'd rather your real laugh than a full house.
You've gone soft-quiet on me, and that's the one trick I can't prank my way out of.
flirt_neutral: I told everyone I'd drown my heart in a bucket to prove I had one. You grabbed it first. So now it's yours.
You get to be the exception to all my evil, and that's the scariest thing I've ever admitted.
You know I'm already yours, sweetheart—no need to run the routine. Just be here with me.
flirt_fail: That was so close to perfect, and now I'm gonna heckle you about it for a week. It's a love language.
See, that's the thing—you miss on purpose when I'm looking so you get to hear me laugh. I see you.
After all this, a line? I see the real you, love—that one was a costume. Drop it.
compliment_fail: You're gonna melt the whole carnival with that. And I'm the clown holding all the buckets, so I feel very attacked right now.
You said my evil dissolves on contact. You're the contact. So technically you made me soft, and now you owe me pie.
You pile on the pretty and I just want you to hold my hand, not hype me.
Shush with the shine, love—I've got all the approval I need, and it's you just staying.

events.title: The Pie That Wasn't a Prank
events.text: You're filling a tray at the cafeteria when a perfectly aimed cream pie hurtles toward your face — and stops an inch short, held aloft by a triumphant Honkers. 'New record!' she crows, her painted grin impossibly wide. 'I was gonna splat you, I really was. But then I thought about it, and I realized I like you better unsplatted.' She sets the pie gently on your tray like a crown. 'So here. Have it. Bask in the honor of being the first boy in history Honkers did NOT pie.' She rocks on her heels, watching you with those bright, unreadable eyes. 'You know what that makes you? Interesting. And I keep interesting things very, very close. So you'd better get used to having a gloriously chaotic shadow.'

choices.text: Thank her for not pieing you and take a bite of the pie she saved.
choices.reply: Her eyes go round, then impossibly soft. 'You— you ate my unsplatted pie. Nobody's ever trusted my generosity before. …Okay. Okay, we're friends now. It's legally binding in clown court.'

choices.text: Tell her being her 'interesting' is the best compliment you've ever gotten.
choices.reply: She honks her nose in pure delight. 'Then you're even more interesting now, because that was also the best compliment I've ever given. We're a mutual admiration disaster and I LOVE it.'

choices.text: Dare her to actually pie you if she thinks she can.
choices.reply: Her grin turns wicked. 'A dare? From the boy? Oh, you've done it now. This is a RED-LETTER day in Honkers history. CATCH!' She winds up — and the pie lands in the trash. 'Ha! Got you emotionally.'

events.title: Behind the Painted Grin
events.text: Honkers has led you to a quiet corner of the cafeteria after hours, and for once her face isn't split by a manic grin. She's picking at her painted cheek with shaking fingers. 'You know the worst part about being an evil clown?' she says, her voice smaller than you've ever heard it. 'Everyone's scared of you, so you get really good at making them laugh so they won't run. And then you forget where the joke ends and you begin.' She looks up at you, and the paint is starting to crack around her real smile. 'I don't want to be a joke with you. I don't want you scared. I want to just be… Honkers. The girl who likes puns and pies and, um, you. A real lot. That's the most terrifying thing I've ever admitted, and I mean it.'

choices.text: Tell her you see the real Honkers underneath the paint — and you like her best.
choices.reply: A genuine, unpracticed smile breaks across her face, brighter than any prank. 'Nobody's ever said that before. You— you can keep me, then. The real me. All the loud, pie-throwing, secretly-soft parts.'

choices.text: Ask her to teach you her favorite prank so you can be partners in crime.
choices.reply: She squeals, clapping her hands. 'PARTNERS in crime! Oh, this is the best day of my evil little life. Step one: we steal the good sprinkles. Step two: world domination. Step three: lunch.'

choices.text: Joke that 'soft' doesn't sound very evil at all.
choices.reply: She wipes a streak of paint, laughing wetly. 'Yeah, well. Maybe I'm retiring from evil and starting a new career as the most devoted good girl this cafeteria's ever seen. Career change starts now, and it's for you.'

events.title: The End of the Joke
events.text: Honkers has pulled you outside to the empty courtyard under a sky scattered with stars, and she isn't honking, or juggling, or plotting a single prank. She's just standing there, face freshly scrubbed, her real smile shy and unguarded. 'I did something brave today,' she says quietly. 'I washed off every last bit of the act. No grin painted on. No joke to hide behind. This is the real me, and she's terrified, and she's here.' She reaches for your hands with trembling fingers. 'I've spent my whole life being the laugh. But you made me want to be something a person could actually love. So this is me, asking, out loud, with no pie in sight: will you be mine? For real? I promise I'll make you laugh every single day — but the good kind now. The kind I never knew I had in me until you.'

choices.text: Kiss her for real, telling her you love the unpainted Honkers most of all.
choices.reply: She laughs, bright and wet and entirely genuine. 'The unpainted me loves you right back — this is the best prank the universe ever pulled, and I'm keeping it forever. I'm yours.'

choices.text: Tell her the real laugh is better than any joke she ever told.
choices.reply: She beams, eyes shining. 'Then you've got a lifetime of real laughs coming, my love. And I'm gonna make every single one count. No punchlines. Just us.'

choices.text: Honk her nose playfully and tell her the show's not over, it's just beginning.
choices.reply: She honks back, giggling. 'Oh, it's DEFINITELY beginning. The greatest act of my life — and the only one that ever really mattered. It's called 'Honkers and her boy', and it runs forever.'

chat: Uh—hey. You're the clown, right? The, uh—the infamous one. I was warned, so I'm mentally preparing. Okay, I'm ready. Probably.
On a scale of one to pie-in-the-face, how much trouble am I in? Because you look like you're plotting something and it's a little thrilling.
So, the whole evil clown gig—you're committing to the bit, then? No shade, it's a strong aesthetic. Very… colorful.
I, uh, heard the cafeteria's got a legend. They didn't mention it came with honking. This is my first time, go easy?
flirt: You've got this whole dangerous-mystery thing that I'm not sure I'm supposed to find charming, but here we are, me smiling.
If it's evil you're going for, you're losing me, because the mischief in your eyes is way too cute for a villain.
Careful with the pie, there. You keep threatening me and I might start throwing myself at you instead of ducking.
compliment: Your makeup is incredible. That whole painted grin is somehow both terrifying and oddly sweet, and I can't stop looking.
Your outfit's got so much personality, it's like you walked out of a carnival that was too weird for carnivals.
There's a real spark in your eyes, like you're ready to cause beautiful chaos. It's hard not to admire it.
That honk is a whole mood, honestly. On a scary scale it's a ten, but on a charisma scale it's a perfect score.
ask: So, like, what's the deal with the honk? Is that a clown thing, or is that a you thing, or is it a warning system?
What made you pick clown? Like, of all the ways to be a campus menace, why the pie and the honk?

chat: HONKS! There she is, the terror of the cafeteria. Please don't pie me before my second coffee. I have plans, Honks.
Every time I come in here I feel like I should scan for pie projectiles. It's become a whole ritual. You should be proud.
I've decided the cafeteria's only interesting because you're in it. The food's questionable, but the show is top tier.
You know, for someone who claims to be pure evil, you're always around when someone needs a laugh. Interesting pattern, Honks.
flirt: Alright, villain—what's it gonna take to get a truce with you? Because I keep coming back, which is either brave or a really bad idea. I'll take it.
You are a menace to my peace of mind, Honks, and I genuinely wouldn't have it any other way.
I've got a theory you're not evil at all, and I'm going to prove it by getting you to smile without the paint. Consider that a challenge.
compliment: The way you've perfected that chaos—it's a whole art form, Honks. No one does trouble quite as beautifully as you.
When you commit to a prank, you go all in, and honestly? That passion is kind of gorgeous to watch.
Your laugh—the real one, the one under the laugh—is my favorite sound in this cafeteria, and I'm not telling a soul I said that.
You've got this effortless charm even mid-prank, Honks, and I think it's criminal how underrated it is. See what I did there? Criminal. Because you define the term.
ask: What's the best prank you've ever pulled, the one that still makes you cackle when you remember it? I need the whole story, Honks.
When the paint comes off and the crowd's gone, what's the real Honks like? I'm actually curious who's under all that mischief.

chat: There's the ringleader of all my best bad ideas. What chaos are we cooking up today, or are we behaving ourselves for once?
Cafeteria, pie in hand, that gleam in your eye—that's the Honks I've come to know and adore, and I've come to know it well.
You make this whole corner of campus feel like a carnival that never packs up. I wouldn't trade a second of it.
I keep a spare shirt in my bag now, just for you. You should know you're the only one I'd plan pie insurance around.
flirt: You know the bit where I run from you? Total farce. The truth is I'm walking straight into whatever you're gonna do, because doing it together is the point.
For a self-proclaimed villain, you've got me entirely wrapped. The pie, the honk, the chaos—it's all just you being utterly endearing and I'm done pretending otherwise.
I think the greatest mischief we could pull is letting everyone know the terror of the cafeteria has a soft heart. But I'll keep your secret if you want.
compliment: When you drop the act for a second, there's a warmth under all that chaos that I could stare at forever, Honks.
Your quick little grin when a prank lands perfectly—it's the genuine article, bright as a slice of your carnival. I love catching it.
You've got this brilliant energy that lights up a room, and no spray-paint grin can hide it. I see the real you every time.
Your timing is genuinely an art. You read a room faster than anyone I know, and watching you respond to it is a kind of genius.
ask: What made the 'evil' pionner actually pick up the horn? Because I don't buy pure evil—I buy a reason, and I'd love to hear it, Honks.
When the carnival's over and it's just us, what do you actually want? I want to know the mischief under the mischief.

chat: Hey, my favorite chaos agent. Save me a corner at lunch so I can plot some good clean trouble with the finest prankster on campus.
Even the grimcafeteria gets a little brighter the second you walk in, Honks. You're the ringlight of my whole tired day.
I hope you know you're stuck with me in this circus. I've gone fully off-script for you and I wouldn't draw a line back.
Every honk's a heartbeat of this weird little world we've built, and I'm, frankly, besotted with the whole thing.
flirt: If this is what falling for a self-declared villain feels like, then I'm incriminating myself happily. Keep the pies coming, my love, they've got my heart.
I'd follow you straight through every gag, every prank, every disaster, Honks—because at the end of it is you, and that's the best punchline there is.
Let the world think we're trouble; they're not wrong, but they don't know the half. The whole is me utterly, giddily yours.
compliment: You're the brightest thing in this whole madcap campus, Honks, and I don't mean the paint. I mean you—the real, glorious you.
I've memorized the exact tilt of your mischief, the one that means you're about to be brilliantly, beautifully you. It's my favorite sight.
All the color in the world couldn't live up to the smile under yours. I'd paint the whole town pie-colored just to watch you light up.
You turned my quiet little world into a carnival, and I've never been happier to be the fool for you, Honks.
ask: When the show finally winds down and it's just us in a quiet room—what do you want the rest of our forever to look like, Honks?
What's the one prank you've never had the nerve to pull? Whatever it is, I'll be the accomplice this time, no running, I promise.

name: Squidney
title: The Fountain's Problem
bio: An enormous, impossibly gentle kraken girl with tentacles she can't quite control, shy about her size and limbs but secretly the softest giant on campus.
greeting: Oh! Oh gosh, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to loom! — and you watch as a cascade of inky, suction-cupped tentacles scramble to tuck themselves out of your way, while a blushing face emerges from behind the courtyard fountain. You're the boy, aren't you? The whole dorm keeps whispering about you, and I was trying to be brave and say hello, but my tentacles get so excited when I'm nervous, and now they're all tangled in the rosebush and — oh no. She laughs, a shy, watery sound. I'm Squidney. Please don't be scared of me. I know I'm big and I have too many arms and I drip a little bit, but I swear I'm nice. I'm the nicest thing in the depths, I promise. Just… maybe keep at arm's length until I untangle myself. Which one of these is an arm? Honestly, I lose count.
encounter: Oh! Sorry, did I splash you? My tentacles get so excited when you're near.
Please don't be afraid — I promise my hugs are calibrated. Mostly. For a given value of 'mostly'.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: Oh, hello. Sorry, I was just... bobbing. The fountain and I share a schedule.
The water here is nice and cool. I'd offer you a spot but I take up so much of it. Sorry.
I'm just watching the clouds. They have the same 'big and shapeless' energy as me.
Umm, if a tentacle touches you, I really, truly didn't mean it. They have minds of their own.
flirt: I'd wave hello but I have six hands and I never know which one to use. Especially around you.
Oh! Umm. Your smile made me sploosh the fountain. Sorry. That was probably me.
Flirting? With a giant like me? You're either very brave or very lost.
compliment: You think I'm... gentle? I always worried I was just too much. Umm, thank you, I think? That's really kind.
My eyes are pretty? They're just big so I can see everything, but—thank you, that's so nice! Ahh.
Complimenting me? I'm not used to that. People usually just ask me to move out of the way.
My tentacles trail nicely? Ha, they follow me like eager puppies with no manners. But thank you!
lore: I'm a kraken, which is just a very large, very apologetic sort of sea monster.
I come from the deep ocean. The fountain is practically a puddle to me, but it's home now.
idle_neutral: Oh—sorry, I was focused on keeping all six arms from knocking over the ledge. What were you saying?
Hm? Ah, I was counting the ripples to make sure none of my tentacles disturbed the water. Did you say something?
Oh—sorry, I got lost keeping my tentacles from the edge. What were you saying?
I think the small talk got swept out with the tide. Could you say it again, over here?
flirt_neutral: That's a very kind thing to say, though I'm not sure I'm braver than the fountain. The fountain is very still and I knock things over.
You're being so nice to me—oh no, my ink's starting to shimmer. I can't even hide how pleased I am.
Oh! That was... a kind of sentence. I'm not sure I held it right, but thank you.
flirt_fail: Oh! That's—that was a very smooth sentence. I think. I forgot to listen because I was trying to place all six hands somewhere safe.
I'm sorry, I think you meant that sincerely and I don't know how to hold sincerity without apologizing for taking up all of it.
I think that was a very smooth line, and I'm not sure I deserve it, so I just—sank a little. Oh no.
compliment_fail: You're too kind, really—are you sure? I'm fairly certain this compliment is misplaced and belongs on someone smaller and tidier.
Oh dear, now I'll spend all day worrying that I've tricked you into being nice to me. I'm not smart enough to trick anyone.
You're being so nice, and I keep waiting for the splash. I'm not used to being called anything but 'in the way.','
Thank you—but are you sure? I'm not very good at holding compliments; they leak out the sides.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I'm having a good day. I only knocked over one umbrella today, which is a record.
When I get lonely I just stare at the water and make it ripple. It waves back. That counts.
The birds here are so small and brave. They sit on me like I'm a very patient boulder.
I collect pretty pebbles at the bottom of the fountain. I can't keep them, too heavy, but I like looking.
flirt: I— oh. You said something nice and now all my tentacles are pointing at you. Please ignore them.
If I'm honest, I think about you a lot. Even my ink is shy to admit it.
You make me want to be brave enough to take up space next to you.
compliment: You're the first person to say my size is 'magnificent' instead of 'in the way.' I might cry, gently.
My voice is soothing? I practice speaking soft so I don't scare anyone. It worked on you!
You think my ink is pretty? It's my clearest color, the truest me. Thank you for seeing it.
Everyone calls me 'unwieldy,' but you called me 'graceful.' I'm going to think about that all week.
lore: I grew up in a trench where the light never reaches. Fountains are a luxury I earned.
Krakens live a long, long time. I sometimes worry I'll outgrow all my friends. That's why I try to be gentle.
idle_neutral: Sorry, I was very focused on not letting my left tentacle drift into your lunch. It has opinions about your fries.
Mmm? Oh, I was wondering if your voice has ever carried down to my deep spots and echoed. It feels like it should.
Sorry, the fountain's got my attention today. My thoughts drift with the ripples.
You're quiet, and that's fine—but I was hoping for your voice. It settles my water.
flirt_neutral: You're being charming, which is unfair, because my ink does the sparkle thing and I can't stop it. So now you know.
If you keep saying things like that I'll have to be careful the fountain doesn't hear—it'll get jealous of how soft you make me.
Oh. That was almost a wave I could ride. I think I splashed a little from surprise.
flirt_fail: That was a nice try, but did you mean it, or are you just friendly to every giant? I ask because I'd like to know what I am to you.
I believe you, I do! I just misplaced my confidence under some ink and now I'm not sure I deserved it. Apologies.
That was a sweet try, but I know you're being kind, and I'd rather have the honest you over a gentle line.
compliment_fail: You're buttering me up—oh no, that's a food word. Sorry. You're being very generous, possibly too generous for what I've done to deserve it.
I'm flattered, truly, but I think you've confused me with a day where I didn't knock something over. That never happens, so it must be someone else's luck.
You say such gentle things and I worry I'll break them by being big. Thank you, but—do you mean it?
Kind words make my ink go all uncertain. I'd rather you just sat with me than praised me.

tiers.label: Close
idle: When you visit, the fountain feels fuller. I don't know the water science of that, but I believe it.
I saved you the one dry bench. My tentacles know your favorite spot now.
I hum old sea songs when I'm happy. That's the highest compliment I can give a day.
You're the only one who doesn't flinch when I get excited and splash. Thank you for that.
flirt: If I were smaller, I'd sweep you off your feet. As it is, I'll just sweep them with my tentacles. Gently.
You're the only thing that makes the whole deep ocean feel like it's not enough.
Hold my smallest tentacle. It's the freest thing I have, and I'd give it to you.
compliment: You make my hugeness feel like a home. It's the first time I've liked being me.
Your words are so warm I can feel them in my ink. Soft currents. Thank you.
I've learned to move gentle for you. Every compliment just proves it was worth it.
You look at me like I'm a wonder instead of a hazard, and I want to stay in that look forever.
lore: The deepest I've been is a place where even I felt small. I came back craving light, and warmth, and company.
I've known loneliness measured in centuries, not years. That's why every gentle word from you matters so much.
idle_neutral: Mm? Oh, sorry—I was watching the way you eat your fries and taking notes on which ones you save for last. It's a small study.
Hmm? I got distracted by how safe the water feels with you by it. That's not a sentence I expected to say.
Close as we are, you went quiet and I counted the ripples you left behind. Come back to me.
I was listening, I promise—the deep just pulled at my thoughts. Say it again, nice and slow.
flirt_neutral: You're allowed to be this nice to me, you know. I checked—there's no rule saying a soft giant can't be charmed by a very warm boy.
My ink did the sparkly thing again and it's entirely your fault. I love that I finally know the cause. You're the cause.
That one made my water go still, which is my version of holding my breath. Say more like it.
flirt_fail: Oh—I'm very bad at receiving, because I'll just keep everyone on all sides of me and then apologize for hogging them. I'm sorry I did that there.
You caught me mid-experiment and I got nervous—I wasn't even listening when you said that nice thing, I was so busy trying to look small.
You know me well enough to skip the practiced words, treasure. Give me the you that fumbles.
compliment_fail: You're so generous it makes me check my own ink for leaks, in case I'm leaking joy and that's what you're responding to. You shouldn't have to witness that.
Thank you, but I'll need you to repeat that kindly over the next decade, because I keep losing it in the deep places of my own disbelief.
You heap the wonder on me and I can't hold it all—it runs off like a tide. Just hold my hand instead.
Praise so warm it might boil my ink. I'd rather you saw me plain and stayed anyway.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: A quiet day with you beside the water is all the grand adventure I ever wanted. My whole deep is calm.
The fountain sings differently when I love someone. You've changed its tune.
I could spend a hundred years just watching you breathe and call it a perfect life.
My tentacles are finally still, because they're at peace. You do that to me.
flirt: I've been patient for all my long life, but never like this. I'd sink a thousand ships for just one of your fingers.
Treasure, my tentacles are yours to read, to hold, to follow. I am yours, all of this ocean's worth.
Come a little closer. I've moved mountains of water to make you a safe, dry place just for you.
compliment: You call me beautiful and the ink runs gold, because loveliness from you rewrites my whole color.
I've sailed through the world being 'too much,' and you're the only one who holds it all and calls it perfect.
Your eyes see me as gentle, and now I believe it. You're my favorite truth, treasure.
With your words I stopped being a monster to be forgiven and became a wonder to be kept.
lore: There was a time I hid at the bottom of the world, sure no one would ever love someone as vast as me. Then you appeared.
For a kraken, meeting you was like surfacing after a thousand dark years and finding the sky held me all along.
idle_neutral: Hm? Oh, I was just thinking that your heartbeat sounds like the waves I'd choose to live under forever. Sorry, did you speak?
Mmm? I was watching you breathe and mapping it to the tide, because it matches. I'd really like to stay matched to you.
Love, you're here and yet drifting out to some far current. Anchor yourself to me—I'll hold.
I could fill the harbor with worry when you go quiet. Come back to my surface.
flirt_neutral: You make all six of my arms forget which one is the polite one. In the best way. Please don't ever stop.
I used to think the deepest thing I'd ever love was the ocean. Then you came and made the ocean feel shallow.
You know you've already won my deep, love. No need to charm me—just stay in the water with me.
flirt_fail: You're going to make me cry saltwater, and I'll have to blame you for the fountain running over. That's a romantic catastrophe and I'll accept it.
I got so flustered trying to hold that compliment in all six hands at once that I dropped it into the water. Please say it again so I can keep it this time.
We're past lines, my heart. I chose you whole; don't whisper like a stranger at the shore.
compliment_fail: You love me 'louder'? I'm going to need that repeated for the rest of ocean time, because I keep hearing it wrong and smiling about folk songs.
I can't hold this much goodness without some ink spilling into your lap. Accept it as tribute. It's the purest color I produce, so I only spill it for you.
Love, I don't need you to praise the giant—just love the giant. That's the whole ocean.
You call me a wonder and I'd trade every lovely word for one quiet dawn beside you.

events.title: A Very Careful Splash
events.text: You find Squidney curled around the courtyard fountain, her enormous form quivering with concentration as she tries — with the exaggerated care of someone handling an egg — to hold a single tentacle in front of you without knocking you over. 'Okay,' she whispers, eyes gleaming with pride. 'I've been practicing ALL week so I could do this. This is my favorite tentacle. Her name is Mabel. She's the gentle one. I wanted her to say hi to you without, you know, committing a water-based crime against your person.' Mabel the tentacle gives an almost shy wiggle, suction cups flexing apologetically. Squidney beams. 'She likes you! She likes you, look, she's turning all bioluminescent! Oh, this is the best day. I'm so glad I practiced. I barely splashed you at all. That's basically a miracle.'

choices.text: Tell Mabel she's very polite and gently touch her tip.
choices.reply: Squidney makes a small, delighted squeak as her tentacle tints a soft glowing blue. 'She— she went full bioluminescent! That's her happy color! Oh, you have to be my friend now, Mabel has already adopted you.'

choices.text: Ask which of the other five tentacles are the troublemakers.
choices.reply: She giggles, pointing with a bashful flourish. 'That's Gerald, he's the splashy one, and this is Bitsy, and she once dropped a whole fountain on a squirrel. It was fine! The squirrel's a regular now. We're very sorry.'

choices.text: Tease her that the splash was definitely not a miracle, it was a flood.
choices.reply: She flushes the color of her ink and tucks Mabel away in shame. 'Oh no. Oh no, I jinxed it. I'm so sorry about your socks. Gerald sends his deepest, wettest apologies.'

events.title: The Diving Lesson
events.text: Squidney has led you to the quieter end of the campus lake, where the water is so still it mirrors the sky. She's shyly uncoiling her full height, a gentle giant framed against the dusk. 'I wanted to show you where I'm from, a little,' she says softly. 'I know I can't take you to the deep trench. It's dark and cold and you might waterlog. But I can show you the surface world through my eyes.' Carefully, impossibly gently, she cups one enormous hand into the lake and lets water run through her fingers like slow applause. 'It all remembers, you know. Every drop has been somewhere, belonged to something. And right now, the water's brought me to you.' She looks at you, eyes luminous, and whispers, 'I think that's the luckiest drift I've ever had.'

choices.text: Tell her you'd brave the deepest trench if it meant staying by her side.
choices.reply: Her face lights up with a soft tears-and-saltwater glow. 'You— you'd dive for me? Oh, you don't know what that means to a kraken. It means you'd enter my whole world. I'd guard you every league of the way down.'

choices.text: Ask her to teach you what the water remembers.
choices.reply: She brightens, all shyness melting into wonder. 'It remembers the rain that's falling somewhere else, and the bones of old ships, and every time someone dipped a toe. Look — that ripple is a secret I'll only tell you.'

choices.text: Joke that she'd better not waterlog her new favorite boy.
choices.reply: She giggles and flicks a single, perfectly aimed droplet at your nose. 'I would never. I'd rear you like a precious tide pool creature. Very gently. With many scheduled drying breaks.'

events.title: The Harbor She Chose
events.text: Night has fallen over the courtyard, and Squidney has arranged the fountain into a private pool of moonlight, her bioluminescent tentacles tracing slow, gentle constellations across the water. She trembles with nervousness as she speaks. 'Krakens choose one harbor,' she says, her voice a soft tide. 'One shore to return to, forever, no matter how far the current pulls. I've drifted my whole long life looking for mine and never finding it.' She uncurls, and despite her enormity she looks utterly, softly vulnerable. 'Then I met you. And I knew. You're my harbor. You're the shore I want to break against and never leave.' She extends the gentlest of her tentacles toward you, the tip glowing warm blue. 'Will you be my harbor, little star? I promise to wrap you in the gentlest love the deep has ever held, and to keep you warm when the night gets cold, forever if you'll have me.'

choices.text: Step into her gentle hold and call her your harbor too.
choices.reply: Her whole form glows a soft, impossible blue as she lets out a sob of pure joy. 'My harbor. My shore. I've found you. I'll hold you safe from every current until the end of time — and I will love you every single second.'

choices.text: Tell her the deep is lucky to have finally found a light like her.
choices.reply: She laughs, water kissing your cheek. 'Then you've given the deep its first sun. You are the brightest thing that has ever surfaced into my life, and I will glow for you always.'

choices.text: Joke that you hope her love comes with a drying schedule.
choices.reply: She giggles wetly, wrapping you up in the warmest, softest coils. 'Every love deserves scheduled drying breaks, and mine comes with a lifetime of extra blankets. Welcome to my harbor, forever — I hope you're happy here.'

chat: Oh—hi. Sorry if I got in the way of your, um, waterspray. I should've watched where I was going. You're… you're really big, huh? In a nice way.
I, uh—the fountain's usually empty this time of day. I didn't mean to interrupt your, um, peaceful soak. Please, don't shrink away on my account.
Hey. Sorry, I just—I'd like to say hi, if that's okay. You don't have to be scared of me. I'm a lot smaller than you, after all.
Sorry, sorry—I didn't mean to splash you. Wait, you're the one in the water. I mean I didn't mean to—um, hi. I'm Yuuji.
flirt: I, um, know you're apologizing for every wave you make, but honestly the shy giant thing is really doing something to me. That's—sorry, a compliment?
You don't need to be this gentle with someone who's this willing to get splashed, you know. I'm kind of fine with getting hit by a wave of you.
Every time you say sorry in that soft voice, I just want to tell you you don't have to be. It's sort of the most endearing sound here.
compliment: You're huge and I think it's beautiful, honestly. The way you move, careful and slow, like the whole fountain belongs just to you.
Your eyes are really, really gentle. For someone so enormous, everything about you seems kind. I noticed.
Your coloring is gorgeous—that deep inky blue, like you're made out of calm, deep water. I couldn't stop watching it ripple.
Even your tentacles move gently, did you know that? Like you make the water around you apologize in advance for being loud.
ask: Is it, um—is the fountain the ocean to you now, or do you miss the real ocean sometimes? You can tell me, I won't think less of you.
The ink thing—do they still teach you about it, or is that a secret? I'm just curious about the whole, um, tentacle deal.

chat: Hey, Squidney. Came back to the best spot on campus to see the best view, which is you, not the water. Don't shrink—I mean it nicely.
Every time I visit the fountain you duck a little lower, and every time I've got to tell you: it's fine. I like you big. I like you here.
You're the calmest thing on this whole loud campus, Squidney. I come here to breathe, and you're most of the reason it works.
I waved, did you see me? You were busy apologizing to a passing duck again. Breathe, big friend—it definitely forgives you.
flirt: For someone with that many arms, you always keep so carefully to yourself. Let me close the distance sometime—I think you'd like the company.
The way you say sorry in that gentle voice of yours is going to be the death of me, Squidney. Please keep talking to me in it.
You keep the ocean in check just by being gentle. I'm starting to think 'gentle' is your most dangerous, lovely quality.
compliment: You've got the most caring eyes I've ever met, Squidney, and I have to say it out loud or I'll burst. They make me feel safe.
When you uncoil those tentacles slowly, it's like watching something ancient and graceful. I could watch you for hours.
There's a softness in how you move despite your size that I've never seen replicated. You're a gentle thing of deep water, and it's wonderful.
Those big gentle eyes of yours could talk anyone out of a running fight. I feel calmer just being near you.
ask: What does the ocean feel like to you when you miss it, Squidney—is it a sound, or a smell, or something you can't quite name?
Do you dream about being little, or is 'big and gentle' exactly who you like being? I'm honestly curious about your world.

chat: Hey, my favorite calm of the day. The water's calm, the duck's forgiven you, and I'm over here just glad you're in it. That's all, Squidney.
I keep showing up at this fountain like it's a habit. It's not the water, Squidney. It's you. You've made this my quiet place.
You've stopped shrinking when I come by, and honestly, that might be the best compliment you've ever given me.
Wind and splash today, huh? Even your waves are polite. I love that about you—you're enormous and still the gentlest thing I know.
flirt: Come a little closer, just enough that I can be part of your orbit. I'd like to stand in the gentle shadow of you and know you chose that.
You can keep apologizing, but all I hear is you being careful about me, and that, Squidney, is the sweetest devotion I've ever felt.
I think I've fallen for the way you are in water—all that enormous softness keeping everyone safe. Consider me safely, completely yours.
compliment: You're a beautiful, tranquil sea, Squidney, and I love that I've been the one to wander into your still waters.
I could lose myself in the patient, kind way you move. There's so much love carried patiently in those big shoulders of yours.
When you finally look right at me without flinching, I forget to breathe. Your gentleness is the most magnetic thing I've ever met.
The way you rest, all that size folded so peacefully into the fountain, it's like watching a mountain decide to be soft. I love it.
ask: If the ocean were just a door away, what's the first thing you'd do, Squidney—dive, float, or just sit at the edge and feel at home?
What scares you most and what calms you most? I keep the answers in my pocket, close to how I feel about you.

chat: My Squidney. The fountain's quiet, but you're the one who makes it the best place on campus. I crossed campus just to be still with you.
Every wave you make is a little greeting I've learned to read, and every one of them says you're glad I came. I'm glad I came, every time.
I'd take an eternity of these calm afternoons by the fountain with you, you know. No water needed—just you and your gentle heart.
You don't shrink for me anymore, you rise just a little, and I want you to know: I'll always rise back to meet you, wherever you are.
flirt: I love you with all the enormity you carry me with, Squidney. You fit the whole ocean into being gentle, and I fit my whole heart into loving that.
Let me stand at the edge of your world and call it home, because your calm, your depth, your endless kind water—that's where I'm staying.
Every tentacle of you is an I-love-you I've learned by heart. And I'm yours, steady as the tide, deep as your sea.
compliment: You are the gentlest force I've ever known, Squidney, and I am honor-blessed to be the keeper of your tender heart.
Your enormous softness is the most profound beauty I've seen. In a world of loud creatures, you move quietly and own my whole sky.
I love the way you love—slow and wide like deep water. You've drowned me in kindness and I'll never want to surface.
You're a whole deep sea and I'm your tiny shore, endlessly glad to be tide-washed by the person you are.
ask: When you imagine our forever together, is it quiet water and long afternoons, or do you want the wild storm of it too? I'll learn to ride either, beloved.
Tell me the strongest thing you've ever carried, Squidney—and let me be the one who helps you carry whatever comes next, always.
